messages:
kai: Seeing rising ECC + XID rates across us-west1 and us-east2, telemetry is lagging ~3-5m. Autoscaler started evicting nodes, we've lost ~12% capacity in 10m. Anyone else seeing this?
ashley: Yup — dashboards show CE spikes then XID702 resets. telemetry ingestion backlog visible. :eyes:
devon: digging in now. Pattern looks like probe heartbeats are delayed, then CE counters flip to XIDs after retries. Quick snippet from prober logs: `gpu_probe: heartbeat_delay=197s, retried=3, xid=702`
maria: Do we have a list of affected racks/instances? Need to understand blast radius before any mass action.
devon: Aggregating — looks concentrated on racks rack-7[3-9] and rack-8[0-4] in us-west1, plus a few nodes in us-east2. I'll post the full list in a sec.
oncall-bot: drain initiated: node i-0987abcd (rack-73) — reason: repeated XID702 (auto-evac).
tilly: If probes are lagging, autoscaler + eviction loop could be making it worse by constantly cycling capacity. Can we pause auto-evac for nodes that have <10% CE growth to avoid churn?
ashley: Good point. Also seeing that the probe fanout metric spiked to 600 concurrent probes during the window. Might be burst fanout causing telemetry ingestion overload.
devon: Hypothesis: probe fanout -> backlog -> heartbeat lag -> CE counters hit threshold -> firmware resets -> XID. Fix path: throttle probe concurrency and stop mass drains for 15m.
kai: That sounds sensible. Tradeoff: risk leaving a few flaky cards online vs continued capacity loss from churn. What's the quick rollback plan?
maria: Rollback will be immediate: re-enable aggressive drains and revert probe-concurrency to 100% in config.
devon: I'm going to patch probe config for us-west1 as a canary at 25% rollout. Command: ```
PATCH /infra/probes/config
{
  "region": "us-west1",
  "probe_concurrency_factor": 0.25,
  "heartbeat_timeout_sec": 240
}
```
ashley: Can you also open a temp rate limit on prober-to-telemetry (ingest) to prevent backlog? Maybe set ingest-qps=2000 for 20m.
devon: adding ingest rate-limit change to the same rollout.
deploy-bot: config rollouts started: probe-concurrency -> us-west1 (25% nodes), ingest-qps=2000 (20m). Rollout id: r-20260318-77 :rocket:
ashley: I'll pause non-critical burst workloads and notify billing that we'll throttle dedicated burst pools. Expecting cost impact to drop, saves ~ $4-6k/day while we stabilize.
tilly: Also recommend lowering autoscaler aggressiveness (scale_up_threshold -> 0.8) so nodes don't immediately rejoin and retrigger probes.
kai: Do it. Please post the exact commands and confirm once in effect.
devon: Applied: ```
PATCH /infra/autoscaler/config
{
  "scale_up_threshold": 0.8,
  "prevent_immediate_rejoin_seconds": 600
}
```
oncall-bot: autoscaler config applied in us-west1/us-east2. Prevent_immediate_rejoin=600s.
maria: Monitoring: watching ECC/XID counts and capacity. If error rate doesn't drop 50% in 15m we escalate to firmware team and consider rolling firmware rollback on affected rack subset.
kai: Sounds good. Keep updates short here. If telemetry backpressure clears and CE/XID rate subsides we can re-enable bursts after 30m steady state. :thumbsup:
ashley: Noted — notifying product owners + billing.
devon: Initial drop visible already — CE rate down ~35% in the canary region after 6m. Continuing rollout if stable.
maria: I'll create an incident ticket and add notes for postmortem: probe fanout, telemetry backpressure, autoscaler churn amplification, mitigations applied.
ashley: Thanks all.
kai: Great work — tracking. If anyone sees an uptick ping me directly.
